messages:
Maria G: quick question — trying to point the Node SDK at our VPC private endpoint (https://redwood-internal.prod.local) while sitting behind corp proxy. I set REDWOOD_API_HOST=https://redwood-internal.prod.local and HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy.corp:3128 but streaming (server-sent events / chunked) starts then stalls after the first chunk. curl from the bastion to the internal host is fine. anyone run into proxy + private endpoint + streaming quirks?

Sam: we hit similar. usually the culprit is the proxy not doing a proper CONNECT/TLS passthrough for long-lived SSE or the SDK's http agent not using tunnel. Are you using the default fetch/polyfill or node's http(s) agent?

Maria G: Node 18 native fetch via SDK (no extra agent). the stream begins, we get one chunk, then nothing until timeout. logs show socket stays open but no more data.

Leo: two quick checks: 1) try setting NO_PROXY for the internal host so the request skips the corporate proxy (if your network path allows it). 2) if you must go through the proxy, ensure it supports HTTP/1.1 CONNECT and chunked bodies — some proxies buffer until connection close.

Ash: for Node specifically, you can force tunneling with an agent. example:```js
const { HttpsProxyAgent } = require('https-proxy-agent');
const agent = new HttpsProxyAgent('http://proxy.corp:3128');
await fetch(url, { agent, headers: { Host: 'redwood-internal.prod.local' } });```Make sure servername in TLS matches SNI. If the proxy terminates TLS you need the proxy to forward the original Host via CONNECT or use the public hostname in SNI.

Maria G: interesting — can you expand on SNI? our internal cert is for redwood-internal.prod.local, but the proxy rewrites TLS sometimes.

Sam: SNI is the TLS extension that tells the server which cert to present. If the proxy does TLS interception, it will present its own cert and break validation unless you have the proxy CA trusted. If the proxy uses CONNECT tunneling (ideal) then the TLS handshake goes to the destination and SNI stays intact. If it rewrites, streaming can break or chunking may be buffered.

Leo: Python note — requests and urllib3 will use proxy env by default. For streaming with requests you can do `stream=True` and `trust_env=True` but sometimes `trust_env=False` and an explicit proxy adapter with `pool_maxsize` helps. For the Python SDK you can also pass a custom transport that forces connection pooling.

Ash: also confirm Host header vs request URL. Some internal LB setups expect Host header to be the internal DNS name. If you're setting a public hostname in REDWOOD_API_HOST but sending Host: public.example.com, the internal router may route differently. Try explicitly setting header Host: redwood-internal.prod.local as in the snippet.

Maria G: tried agent + explicit Host header — stream looks stable for a minute then stalls again. infra-bot, can you check proxy logs for long-lived connections from my ip?

infra-bot: @Maria G — opened infra ticket INF-8723 and attached the connection samples you posted. Proxy team reported an intermediate buffer threshold at ~16KB that flushes on connection close. They suggested using CONNECT tunneling or switching to a websocket upgrade route.

Sam: OK that explains the single-chunk behavior (proxy buffered the first chunk until the buffer threshold). Two practical options: 1) enable CONNECT/tunnel for the redwood host, or 2) switch the SDK to use websockets for streaming (if your app can accept that). We'll add a note in the devex docs about proxy buffering and the HttpsProxyAgent workaround.

Maria G: sweet — I'll try requesting a tunnel from network and test websockets fallback. if successful I'll paste simple repro and we can shape an SDK doc snippet for Node/Python. thanks y'all :thumbsup:

Ash: also leaving a short checklist for docs: env var names (REDWOOD_API_HOST, REDWOOD_API_KEY, HTTPS_PROXY, NO_PROXY), Node agent example, Python adapter snippet, and a note about SNI/proxy interception. I'll seed a draft in #docs later today.

Maria G: perfect — ping me on the PR for review.
